claim: The second heart field (SHF) is a progenitor population originating in pharyngeal mesoderm that contributes to heart tube elongation through the progressive addition of cells from the dorsal pericardial wall to both poles of the forming heart.
source: The SHF is a progenitor population originating in pharyngeal mesoderm that contributes to heart tube elongation through the progressive addition of cells from the dorsal pericardial wall to both poles of the forming heart.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction describing the SHF based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: The SHF gives rise to right ventricular and outflow tract myocardium at the arterial pole, and to atrial myocardium including the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion (DMP) at the venous pole.
source: The SHF gives rise to right ventricular and outflow tract myocardium at the arterial pole, and to atrial myocardium including the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion (DMP) at the venous pole (Zaffran and Kelly, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work (Zaffran and Kelly, 2012).

claim: Perturbation of SHF cell addition results in impaired heart tube elongation and looping that leads to early embryonic lethality and underlies a spectrum of common congenital heart defects (CHDs).
source: In the absence of SHF cell addition, impaired heart tube elongation and looping leads to early embryonic lethality, and perturbation of this process underlies a spectrum of common congenital heart defects (CHDs) (Prall et al., 2007; Cai et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Prall et al., 2007; Cai et al., 2003).

claim: The SHF is sub-divided into distinct anterior and posterior regions (aSHF and pSHF).
source: Lineage tracing analysis in mammals has revealed that the SHF is sub-divided into distinct anterior and posterior regions (aSHF and pSHF) (Domínguez et al., 2012; Lescroart et al., 2012; Vincent and Buckingham, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to lineage tracing studies.

claim: Cardiac progenitors in the aSHF contribute to the right ventricular and outflow tract myocardium.
source: Cardiac progenitors in the aSHF contribute to the right ventricular and outflow tract myocardium (Buckingham et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Buckingham et al., 2005.

claim: pSHF cells participate in the formation of the atrial and atrioventricular septation through development of the DMP that forms the muscular base of the primary atrial septum.
source: whereas pSHF cells participate to the formation of the atrial and atrioventricular septation through development of the DMP that forms the muscular base of the primary atrial septum (Briggs et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Briggs et al., 2012.

claim: A sub-population of the pSHF contributes to the inferior wall of the outflow tract which gives rise to the myocardium at the base of the pulmonary trunk.
source: In addition, a sub-population of the pSHF has been shown to contribute to the inferior wall of the outflow tract which gives rise to the myocardium at the base of the pulmonary trunk (Bertrand et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bertrand et al., 2011.

claim: Retinoic acid (RA) signaling is required to define the limit between the anterior and posterior SHF.
source: Specifically, RA signaling is required to define the limit between the anterior and posterior SHF, as indicated by the abnormal posterior expansion of the expression of aSHF markers genes, including Fgf8, Fgf10, and Tbx1, in Raldh2-mutant embryos (De Bono et al., 2018; Ryckebusch et al., 2008; Sirbu et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies showing abnormal marker gene expression in Raldh2-mutant embryos.

claim: Hoxa1, Hoxa3 and Hoxb1 are expressed in overlapping sub-populations of cardiac progenitor cells in the pSHF and downregulated prior to differentiation.
source: Hoxa1, Hoxa3 and Hoxb1 are expressed in overlapping sub-populations of cardiac progenitor cells in the pSHF and downregulated prior to differentiation (Bertrand et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bertrand et al., 2011.

claim: Hoxb1- and Hoxa1-expressing progenitor cells located in the pSHF segregate to both cardiac poles, contributing to the inflow tract and the inferior wall of the outflow tract.
source: Hoxb1- and Hoxa1-expressing progenitor cells located in the pSHF segregate to both cardiac poles, contributing to the inflow tract and the inferior wall of the outflow tract (Lescroart and Zaffran, 2018; Bertrand et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cardiac progenitors that contribute to the superior wall of the outflow tract and right ventricle do not express Hox transcription factors.
source: In contrast, cardiac progenitors that contribute to the superior wall of the outflow tract and right ventricle do not express Hox transcription factors.
evidence: This is a direct statement contrasting Hox expression patterns in different cardiac progenitor populations.

claim: Hoxb1 is required for normal deployment of SHF cells during outflow tract development.
source: Hoxb1 is required for normal deployment of SHF cells during outflow tract development (Roux et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Roux et al., 2015.

claim: At E9.5 (16 somites), the GFP reporter of Hoxb1GFP embryos is detectable in the posterior region of the SHF.
source: At embryonic day (E) 9.5 (16 somites [s]), the GFP reporter of Hoxb1GFP embryos is detectable in the posterior region of the SHF (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by direct observation shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Hoxb1 progenitors contribute to both atria, the DMP and the myocardium at the base of the pulmonary trunk at E11.5-E12.5.
source: Genetic lineage analysis of Hoxb1-expressing cells using the Hoxb1IRES-Cre mouse line showed that Hoxb1 progenitors contribute to both atria, the DMP and the myocardium at the base of the pulmonary trunk at E11.5-E12.5 (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic lineage analysis data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: Mef2c-Cre-expressing cells contribute to the great arteries (aorta and pulmonary trunk) and the right ventricle at E12.5.
source: At E12.5, the contribution of Mef2-Cre-expressing cells is observed in the great arteries (aorta and pulmonary trunk) and the right ventricle (Figure 1F), consistent with previous observations (De Bono et al., 2018; Goddeeris et al., 2008; Verzi et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1F and citations to previous studies.

claim: Expression of Osr1, a gene expressed in pSHF progenitors, largely overlaps with Hoxb1 expression at E8.5-9.
source: At E8.5–9, RNA-FISH showed that expression of Osr1, a gene expressed in pSHF progenitors (Zhou et al., 2015), largely overlapped with Hoxb1 expression (Figure 1G and I)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figures 1G and 1I, and a citation to Zhou et al., 2015.

claim: Mef2c-Cre predominantly labels a distinct progenitor cell population from Osr1 at E8.5-9.
source: whereas Mef2c-Cre predominantly labeled a distinct progenitor cell population to Osr1 (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1G and 1H.

claim: A minor subset of cardiac progenitors are co-labeled by Hoxb1 and Mef2c-Cre;RosatdT (Tomato+), likely corresponding to progenitor cells giving rise to the DMP at the venous pole and inferior outflow tract wall at the arterial pole.
source: Double whole-mount in situ hybridization identified a minor subset of cardiac progenitors co-labeled by Hoxb1 and Mef2c-Cre;RosatdT (Tomato+), likely corresponding to progenitor cells giving rise the DMP at the venous pole and inferior outflow tract wall at the arterial pole (Figure 1I–K; Roux et al., 2015; Briggs et al., 2013; Bertrand et al., 2011; Verzi et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by double whole-mount in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 1I-K and citations to previous studies.

claim: Tomato+ and GFP+ cells comprise, respectively, 33% and 23% of the total micro-dissected SHF region at E9.5.
source: FACS analysis showed that Tomato+ and GFP+ cells comprise, respectively, 33% and 23% of the total micro-dissected region (Figure 2B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figures 2B and 2D.

claim: 2,133 genes were transcribed specifically in the GFP+ (Hoxb1-expressing) population.
source: We identified 11,970 genes expressed in both cell types. 2,133 genes were transcribed specifically in the GFP+ population (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis for genes specifically expressed in the GFP+ population showed significant enrichment of GO terms associated with 'heart development', 'epithelium development', 'cardiac chamber morphogenesis' and 'cell adhesion'.
source: Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis for the biological processes linked to these genes showed a significant enrichment of GO terms associated with 'heart development', 'epithelium development', 'cardiac chamber morphogenesis' and 'cell adhesion' (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis results shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Genes previously described as being expressed in the posterior region of the SHF, including Tbx5, Osr1, Tbx18, Foxf1, Wnt2, Bmp4, Nr2f2, Sema3c, and Gata4, were identified in the 'heart development' list of genes specifically expressed in the GFP+ population.
source: Included in the 'heart development' list we identified several genes previously described as being expressed in the posterior region of the SHF (e.g., Tbx5, Osr1, Tbx18, Foxf1, and Wnt2), as well as Bmp4, Nr2f2, Sema3c, Gata4 (Figure 2H- and Figure 2—figure supplement 2; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2, and knowledge of previous studies.

claim: Bmp4 is expressed in the pSHF.
source: RNA-FISH analysis validated the expression of Bmp4 in the pSHF (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: 1285 peaks representing open chromatin were exclusively accessible in the GFP+ population.
source: By comparing the signal for each peak in Tomato+ and GFP+ populations, we identified 1285 peaks that were exclusively accessible in the GFP+ population (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Approximately 94% of peaks were found in both the GFP+ and Tomato+ populations, while 3.5% of the peaks were exclusively present in the GFP+ population.
source: Approximately 94% of peaks found in both the GFP+ and Tomato+ populations, while 3.5% of the peaks were exclusively present in the GFP+ population (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 53 peaks in the Tomato+ population and 65 peaks in the GFP+ population correlated with changes in gene expression.
source: However, we found 53 (Tomato+ population) and 65 (GFP+ population) peaks correlating with changes in gene expression (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: There is an over-representation of TSS in the 'GFP+' peaks compared to the 'Tomato+' peaks suggesting that genes with open promoters are preferentially activated in the pSHF.
source: Interestingly, we observed an over-representation of TSS in the 'GFP+' peaks compared to the 'Tomato+' peaks suggesting that genes with open promoters are preferentially activated in the pSHF (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and represents an inference from the data.

claim: ATAC-seq data for the GFP+ population revealed a high read count around the promoter regions of genes enriched in the pSHF, including Hoxb1, Aldh1a2, Osr1 and Sema3c.
source: ATAC-seq data for the GFP+ population thus revealed a high read count around the promoter regions of genes enriched in the pSHF, including Hoxb1, Aldh1a2, Osr1 and Sema3c (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 3F-H.

claim: The pSHF enhancer previously identified at the Foxf1a locus exhibited enrichment of ATAC-seq reads in GFP+ population.
source: Similarly, the pSHF enhancer previously identified at the Foxf1a locus (Hoffmann et al., 2014) exhibited enrichment of ATAC-seq reads in GFP+ population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F and a citation to Hoffmann et al., 2014.

claim: The established Mef2c anterior heart field enhancer (Mef2c-F6; 285 bp) was marked by open chromatin in the Tomato+ population, but not the GFP+ population.
source: In contrast, the established Mef2c anterior heart field enhancer (Mef2c-F6; 285 bp) (Dodou et al., 2004) was marked by open chromatin in the Tomato+ population, but not the GFP+ population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F and a citation to Dodou et al., 2004.

claim: One of the most highly enriched motifs in open chromatin regions of the GFP+ population was the consensus HOX motif.
source: One of the most highly enriched motif in open chromatin regions of the GFP+ population was the consensus HOX motif (Figure 3I; Fan et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3I and a citation to Fan et al., 2012.

claim: Other significantly enriched motifs in open chromatin regions of the GFP+ population include putative binding sites for PBX and MEIS proteins.
source: Other significantly enriched motifs include putative binding sites for PBX and MEIS proteins (Figure 3I)
evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The most enriched combinations of motifs in pSHF candidate enhancers contained HOX motifs adjacent to TALE transcription factor recognition sequences.
source: Our computational analysis showed that the most enriched combinations contained HOX motifs adjacent to TALE transcription factor recognition sequences.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis of motif combinations.

claim: In open chromatin regions of the Tomato+ population there was enrichment of motifs for RUNX, LHX and TEAD transcription factors.
source: In open chromatin regions of the Tomato+ population we observed enrichment of motifs for RUNX, LHX and TEAD transcription factors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos exhibited severe heart defects as early as E9.5, including a looping defect and common ventricular chamber.
source: Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos exhibited severe heart defects as early as E9.5, as observed by a looping defect and common ventricular chamber in transgenic compared to control embryos (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by macroscopic observations shown in Figures 4A-B.

claim: At E10.5, Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos had an abnormally shaped heart with no clear distinction between right and left ventricular chambers.
source: However, in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos, the heart was abnormally shaped with no clear distinction between right and left ventricular chambers (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: At E12.5, Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos showed a hypoplastic right ventricle with abnormal positioning of the ventricular septum.
source: The phenotype was even more pronounced at E12.5, when Hematoxylin and Eosin-stained transverse sections showed a hypoplastic right ventricle with abnormal positioning of the ventricular septum (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: Hypoplasia of the right ventricle in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos was evident at E15.5 (8/8 embryos).
source: Hypoplasia of the right ventricle in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos was evident at E15.5 (Figure 4G–J; 8/8).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4G-J with quantification (8/8 embryos).

claim: At E15.5, an abnormally thin right ventricular wall was observed in 5/8 Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos.
source: At this stage, an abnormally thin right ventricular wall was observed (5/8).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of the phenotype in 5 out of 8 embryos.

claim: 50% of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos showed misalignment of the great arteries (4/8).
source: In addition, 50% of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos showed misalignment of the great arteries (4/8)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of the phenotype in 4 out of 8 embryos.

claim: 63% of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos displayed ventricular septal defects (VSD; 5/8).
source: and 63% displayed ventricular septal defects (VSD; 5/8).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of the phenotype in 5 out of 8 embryos.

claim: No viable Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre pups with hypoplastic right ventricle were observed.
source: In this context, we never observed viable Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre pups with hypoplastic right ventricle.
evidence: This is a direct observation of the absence of viable pups with the phenotype.

claim: A striking reduction of the β-gal+ expression domain was observed in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre;R26R embryos compared to control embryos at E9.5.
source: In contrast, a striking reduction of the β-gal+ expression domain was observed in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre;R26R embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Quantitative analysis demonstrated a reduction of the β-gal+ expression domain in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre;Mlc1v24 compared to control embryos.
source: Quantitative analysis demonstrated a reduction of the β-gal+ expression domain in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre;Mlc1v24 compared to control embryos consistent with a reduction of the distance between the arterial and venous poles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G-J.

claim: There was a modest reduction in cell proliferation between control and Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos at E9.5.
source: There was a modest reduction in cell proliferation between control and Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos (Figure 4K–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figures 4K-M.

claim: A significant increase of Caspase-3 and TUNEL-positive cells was detected in the aSHF (Isl1+) of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre compared to control embryos, indicating increased apoptosis.
source: However, a significant increase of Caspase-3 and TUNEL-positive cells was detected in the aSHF (Isl1+) of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre compared to control embryos, indicating increased apoptosis (Figure 4N–Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figures 4N-Q.

claim: The severe right ventricular hypoplasia resulting from ectopic Hoxb1 expression was primarily due to extensive cell death and secondarily to reduced proliferation in the aSHF.
source: Hence, the severe right ventricular hypoplasia resulting from ectopic Hoxb1 expression was primarily due to extensive cell death and secondarily to reduced proliferation in the aSHF.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell death and proliferation data presented.

claim: At E9.5, Hoxb1GoF;Hoxb1-Cre hearts were indistinguishable from those of control embryos.
source: At E9.5, Hoxb1GoF;Hoxb1-Cre hearts were indistinguishable from those of control embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-mount in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Gross morphological observations of E13.5 hearts did not reveal any difference in Hoxb1GoF;Hoxb1-Cre compared to control embryos.
source: Similarly, gross morphological observations of E13.5 hearts did not reveal any difference in Hoxb1GoF;Hoxb1-Cre compared to control embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C-D.

claim: Over-expression of Hoxb1 in the pSHF does not lead to heart defects.
source: These data suggest that over-expression of Hoxb1 in the pSHF does not lead to heart defects, and that the phenotypes observed in the Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos result from misexpression in aSHF progenitor cells that normally do not express Hoxb1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of Hoxb1GoF;Hoxb1-Cre and Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre phenotypes.

claim: 1378 genes were upregulated and 1345 genes were downregulated in the SHF of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos compared to controls.
source: We identified 1378 genes upregulated and 1345 genes downregulated in the SHF of Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis.

claim: GO enrichment analysis for upregulated genes in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos showed significant enrichment of the GO terms 'cell death' and 'apoptotic signaling pathway'.
source: GO enrichment analysis for the biological processes associated with the upregulated genes showed significant enrichment of the GO terms 'cell death' and 'apoptotic signaling pathway' (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–D)
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: GO analysis of downregulated genes in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos revealed an enrichment in the GO terms 'heart development' and 'muscle cell differentiation' suggesting an inhibition of cardiac differentiation.
source: GO analysis of the downregulated genes revealed an enrichment in the GO terms 'heart development' and 'muscle cell differentiation' suggesting an inhibition of cardiac differentiation (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, with an inference about inhibition of differentiation.

claim: Fgf10, a well-characterized marker of the aSHF, was among the most significant downregulated genes in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos (p=0.002).
source: Fgf10, a well-characterized marker of the aSHF (Kelly et al., 2001), was among the most significant downregulated genes in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos (p=0.002) (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, with a citation to Kelly et al., 2001.

claim: Osr1 and Tbx5, known to regulate cell cycle progression in the pSHF, were upregulated in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos.
source: Among the upregulated genes, we found Osr1 and Tbx5, known to regulate cell cycle progression in the pSHF (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E; Supplementary file 1; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E, and a citation to Zhou et al., 2015.

claim: The pSHF markers Tbx5 and Osr1 are both expressed in the GFP+ cells in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos, indicating that the ectopic expression of Hoxb1 in the Mef2c-AHF+ domain alters cardiac progenitor cell identity.
source: Moreover, we found that the pSHF markers Tbx5 and Osr1 are both expressed in the GFP+ cells in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos, indicating that the ectopic expression of Hoxb1 in the Mef2c-AHF+ domain alters cardiac progenitor cell identity (Figure 5E,E'–K,K'').
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figures 5E-K, with an inference about altered cell identity.

claim: An anterior shift in expression of the pSHF gene Nr2f2 was observed in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos.
source: Similarly to Tbx5 and Osr1, we observed an anterior shift in expression of the pSHF gene Nr2f2 in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1G.

claim: 249 genes were upregulated and 292 genes were downregulated in Hoxb1-/- embryos compared to wild-type.
source: We identified 249 genes upregulated, and 292 genes downregulated in Hoxb1-/- embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis.

claim: GO term analysis of upregulated genes in Hoxb1-/- embryos revealed a significant enrichment of terms including 'heart development', 'cardiac muscle tissue development' and 'regulation of cell differentiation'.
source: Interestingly, GO term analysis of the upregulated genes revealed a significant enrichment of terms including 'heart development', 'cardiac muscle tissue development' and 'regulation of cell differentiation' (Figure 5M and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5M and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C-D.

claim: Upregulation of several myocardial-specific genes (e.g., Myl2, Myh7, Actn2, Myl3, Nppa (Anf), and Nppb (Bnf)) indicates premature cardiac differentiation in the SHF of Hoxb1-/- mutant embryos.
source: Upregulation of several myocardial-specific genes (e.g., Myl2, Myh7, Actn2, Myl3, Nppa (Anf), and Nppb (Bnf)), indicates a premature cardiac differentiation in the SHF of Hoxb1-/- mutant embryos (Figure 5N; Figure 5—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5N and Figure 5—figure supplement 3E, with an inference about premature differentiation.

claim: The GO term 'epithelial cell development' was significantly enriched in the downregulated genes in Hoxb1-/- embryos.
source: The GO term 'epithelial cell development' was significantly enriched in the downregulated genes (e.g., Cdh1, Llgl2, and Lrp5) (Figure 5M and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C–D)
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5M and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C-D.

claim: The relative length of the Tbx1+ region close to the outflow tract revealed a significant reduction in the size of the Tbx1+ versus Tbx5+ domains in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos.
source: In Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre embryos the relative length of the Tbx1+ region close to the outflow tract revealed a significant reduction in the size of the Tbx1+ versus Tbx5+ domains (Figure 6A,B)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Measurement of the length of each domain revealed that the Tbx1+ domain was significantly reduced in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre compared to Mef2c-Cre (control) embryos.
source: Measurement of the length of each domain revealed that the Tbx1+ domain was significantly reduced in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre compared to Mef2c-Cre (control) embryos (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Despite a general reduction of the SHF, the Tbx5+ domain is increased in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre compared to control embryos.
source: In addition, despite a general reduction of the SHF, the Tbx5+ domain is increased in Hoxb1GoF;Mef2c-Cre compared to control embryos (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The Tbx5+ domain appears slightly shorter in Hoxb1-/- embryos than in Hoxb1+/- littermates.
source: The Tbx5+ domain appears slightly shorter in Hoxb1-/- embryos than in Hoxb1+/- littermates (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 6E and 6F.

claim: The Tbx5+ domain was shorter in double Hoxa1-/-;Hoxb1-/- compared to Hoxb1+/- littermate embryos.
source: We found that the Tbx5+ domain was shorter in double Hoxa1-/-;Hoxb1-/- compared to Hoxb1+/- littermate embryos (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figures 6G and 6H.

claim: Hoxa1-/-;Hoxb1-/- hearts at fetal stages showed lack of the DMP, resulting in a primum type atrial septal defect, a class of AVSD (3/3 embryos).
source: Characterization of cardiac morphology in Hoxa1-/-;Hoxb1-/- hearts at fetal stages revealed lack of the DMP, a posterior SHF derivative, resulting in a primum type atrial septal defect, a class of AVSD (3/3; Figure 6I,J).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figures 6I and 6J with quantification (3/3 embryos).

claim: Inappropriate differentiation of SHF cells may contribute to the loss of DMP formation in Hoxa1-/-;Hoxb1-/- mutants.
source: Inappropriate differentiation of SHF cells may contribute to the loss of DMP formation in these mutants, providing the first evidence that Hoxa1 and Hoxb1 are required for atrioventricular septation.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed phenotype and previous findings.

claim: A peak of Hoxb1 expression was detected at day 4-5 during cardiac differentiation of mES cells, just before the onset of cardiac differentiation.
source: Using a time-course gene expression analysis during cardiac differentiation of mES cells, we detected a peak of Hoxb1 expression at day 4–5 just before the onset of cardiac differentiation (Figure 7B)
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The peak of Hoxa1 expression was detected after day 5 during cardiac differentiation of mES cells.
source: Consistent with the initial activation of Hoxb1 and Hoxa1 during heart development in the mouse (Bertrand et al., 2011), the peak of Hoxa1 expression was detected after day 5 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7B and a citation to Bertrand et al., 2011.

claim: Permanent DOX (1 or 0.2 μg/ml) treatment from day 4 of direct cardiac induction onwards interfered with the differentiation process of cardiac cells as shown by specific downregulation of the expression of Myh7, Myh6, Mlc2a, and Mlc2v.
source: Permanent DOX (1 or 0.2 μg/ml) treatment from day 4 of direct cardiac induction onwards (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2) interfered with the differentiation process of cardiac cells as shown by specific downregulation of the expression of Myh7, Myh6, Mlc2a, and Mlc2v (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: A decreased number of beating embryoid bodies (EBs) was found after DOX treatment.
source: Accordingly, in these conditions, we found a decreased number of beating embryoid bodies (EBs) (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Reduction of beating EBs after Hoxb1 induction was not caused by ES cell apoptosis.
source: Absence of upregulation of cell death markers attested that reduction of beating EBs was not caused by ES cell apoptosis (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data for apoptosis markers shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Upregulation of Osr1, Tbx5 and Bmp4 expression was observed after Hoxb1 induction in mES cells, suggesting that the cellular identity of differentiating EB cells is changed.
source: Interestingly, we also observed an upregulation of Osr1, Tbx5 and Bmp4 expression under these conditions, suggesting that the cellular identity of differentiating EB cells is changed, consistent with our in vivo observations (Figure 5C–K and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, with an inference about changed cellular identity.

claim: Hoxb1 activation in mES cells results in arrest of cardiac differentiation and failure of proper identity commitment.
source: Therefore, our data suggest that Hoxb1 activation in mES cells results in arrest of cardiac differentiation and failure of proper identity commitment, consistent with in vivo results.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mES cell differentiation data.

claim: RNA-seq data showed a higher read count for Nppa and Nppb in the Hoxb1-/- compared to control embryos.
source: RNA-seq data showed a higher read count for Nppa and Nppb in the Hoxb1-/- compared to control embryos (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: At E9.5, RNA-FISH confirmed an ectopic expression of Nppa in the SHF of Hoxb1-/- and Hoxa1-/-Hoxb1-/- embryos.
source: At E9.5, RNA-FISH confirmed an ectopic expression of Nppa in the SHF of Hoxb1-/- (Figure 8B,C) and Hoxa1-/-Hoxb1-/- (Figure 8D,E) embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figures 8B-E.

claim: Upon Hoxb1 induction, the expression of Nppa and Nppb was downregulated in EBs.
source: In contrast, upon Hoxb1 induction, the expression of Nppa and Nppb was downregulated in EBs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: ChIP-seq data in mouse ES cell lines showed that Hoxa1, a paralog of Hoxb1, and HDAC-1 and -2 bind the Nppa and Nppb loci.
source: ChIP-seq data in mouse ES cell lines had shown that Hoxa1, a paralog of Hoxb1, and HDAC-1 and −2 bind the Nppa and Nppb loci (De Kumar et al., 2017; Whyte et al., 2012; Figure 8G).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8G and citations to De Kumar et al., 2017 and Whyte et al., 2012.

claim: Transfection of Nkx2-5 alone or co-transfection of Nkx2-5 and Gata4 resulted in strong activation of the 0.7 kb Nppa promoter in both Cos-7 and NIH3T3 cells.
source: As described (Durocher et al., 1997), transfection of Nkx2-5 alone or co-transfection of Nkx2-5 and Gata4 resulted in strong activation of the 0.7 kb Nppa promoter containing an HOX-motif in both Cos-7 and NIH3T3 cells (Figure 8I and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8I and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, and a citation to Durocher et al., 1997.

claim: The activity of the 0.7 kb Nppa promoter decreased three-fold upon co-transfection with a Hoxb1 expression vector or co-transfection of Hoxb1 and Hoxa1.
source: However, this activity decreased three-fold upon co-transfection with a Hoxb1 expression vector or co-transfection of Hoxb1 and Hoxa1, which are co-expressed in pSHF progenitor cells in vivo (Figure 8I), demonstrating the repressive role of Hoxb1 on the 0.7 kb Nppa promoter.
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: HDACs inhibition increased the luciferase activity of the Nppa reporter constructs.
source: HDACs inhibition increased the luciferase activity of the reporter constructs (Figure 8J and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data with TSA treatment shown in Figure 8J and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: When co-transfected, Hoxb1 or Hoxa1 suppressed the TSA-mediated activation of the Nppa promoter in cell culture.
source: When co-transfected, Hoxb1 or Hoxa1 suppressed the TSA-mediated activation of the Nppa promoter in cell culture (Figure 8J).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8J.

claim: RNA-seq data showed a higher read count for Tnnt2 in the Hoxb1-/- compared to control embryos.
source: As for Nppa and Nppb, RNA-seq data showed a higher read count for Tnnt2 in the Hoxb1-/- compared to control embryos (Figure 8F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: ChIP-seq dataset showed that Hoxb1 as well as Meis1 bind to the Tnnt2 locus.
source: Analysis of ChIP-seq dataset showed that Hoxb1 as well as Meis1 bind to the Tnnt2 locus (Figure 8H).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: Co-transfection with a Hoxb1 expression vector or co-transfection of Hoxb1 and Hoxa1 suppressed TSA-medicated activation of the Tnnt2 promoter in Cos7 cells.
source: As in the case of the Nppa promoter we observed that co-transfection with a Hoxb1 expression vector or co-transfection of Hoxb1 and Hoxa1 suppressed TSA-medicated activation of the Tnnt2 promoter in Cos7 cells (Figure 8J).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8J.

claim: Hoxb1 inhibits differentiation in the pSHF by directly repressing myocardial gene transcription even under conditions of histone acetylation.
source: Together these results suggest that Hoxb1 inhibits differentiation in the pSHF by directly repressing myocardial gene transcription even under conditions of histone acetylation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the luciferase reporter assay data with TSA treatment.

claim: Hoxb1 plays a key role in patterning cardiac progenitor cells that contribute to both cardiac poles.
source: Our results show that Hoxb1 plays a key role in patterning cardiac progenitor cells that contribute to both cardiac poles and provide new insights into the pathogenesis of CHD.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on all the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: Hoxb1 negatively regulates differentiation in the posterior SHF.
source: Here, we profile the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility of anterior and posterior SHF sub-populations at genome-wide levels and demonstrate that Hoxb1 negatively regulates differentiation in the posterior SHF.
evidence: This is a summary claim from the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Spatial mis-expression of Hoxb1 in the anterior SHF results in hypoplastic right ventricle.
source: Spatial mis-expression of Hoxb1 in the anterior SHF results in hypoplastic right ventricle.
evidence: This is a summary claim from the abstract based on the gain-of-function experiments.

claim: Hoxb1-deficient mouse embryos display premature cardiac differentiation.
source: whereas Hoxb1-deficient mouse embryos display premature cardiac differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary claim from the abstract based on the loss-of-function experiments.

claim: Ectopic differentiation in the posterior SHF of embryos lacking both Hoxb1 and its paralog Hoxa1 results in atrioventricular septal defects.
source: Moreover, ectopic differentiation in the posterior SHF of embryos lacking both Hoxb1 and its paralog Hoxa1 results in atrioventricular septal defects.
evidence: This is a summary claim from the abstract based on the double mutant analysis.
